SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
1102
20. 9. 41

Section 1. Sp. Br. Station. File No. Date September 19, 1941

SUBJECT: September 18 Anniversary - passed off quietly.

The anniversary of the Mukden Incident (1931), which fell on September 18, passed off quietly without any untoward incident. A small quantity of national salvation literature was surreptitiously disseminated in the Settlement between September 14th and 18th, and some pro-Wang Ching Wei and anti-Foreign handbills made their appearance in the Settlement on September 18th.

On September 15, two male Chinese were arrested by the Police for posting handbills of a national salvation nature in Bubbling Well district and two further arrests were made later. The case against them was still pending at the time this report was compiled.

On September 18, motorcar No. 3798 was stopped by the Police at the Yu Yuen Road barrier when 2,000 copies of a pro-Wang Ching Wei handbill were found in the car and the chauffeur and three occupants were taken into custody.. They were released later the same day.

A list in tabular form of the handbills which came into the possession of the Police on the occasion of the September 18th Anniversary, giving a brief summary of the contents of the literature and the place of distribution, is attached hereto together with specimens of the handbills.

报告
1102
1941年9月20日

第一节。特别处分站。档案号。日期：1941年9月19日

主题：九一八纪念日——平静度过。

1931年“九一八”事变（Mukden Incident）周年纪念日（9月18日）已平静度过，未发生任何意外事件。9月14日至18日期间，租界内有人秘密散发少量救国宣传品；9月18日，租界内出现了一些拥汪精卫及反外人的传单。

9月15日，两名中国男子因在静安寺路地区张贴具有救国性质的传单而被警方逮捕，随后又有两人被捕。在编制本报告时，针对他们的案件仍在审理中。

9月18日，一辆车牌号为3798的汽车在愚园路卡口被警方拦停，车内发现2000份拥汪精卫传单，司机及三名乘客被拘留。他们于同日稍后获释。

随函附上警方在九一八纪念日期间查获的传单清单（表格形式），简要列出了宣传品的内容摘要及散发地点，并附有传单样本。

沉痛的一九一八一紀念，至今已十週年了。在此十
年之中，敵人狼子野心，欲求無，長蛇封豕，食鯨
吞，繼之遂有「一二八」淞滬之役，「七七」蘆溝橋事
變，「八一三」上海戰爭，燃起了全面抗戰的炬火。直
至今日，我同胞，在前線的，拋頭顱，灑熱血；在淪
陷區的，輾轉呻吟，更飽嘗了鐵蹄蹂躪下的非人生活；
而其中忍痛最久茹苦最多的，當推東北四省的同胞。在
此時此際，我們來紀念一九一八一，一方面慶幸我國領
導得人，在賢明的 蔣委員長指揮之下，羣策羣力，艱
苦奮鬥，已博得國際間的同情與援助，造成了勝利在望
的局面；但另一方面我們卻不得不痛惜當時的守土將士
，未能克盡厥職，白山黑水，拱手讓人，啟敵人輕視之
心，致造成今日的不良後果。
當「九一八」事變之初，東北守將張學良將軍，在
事前既未能綢繆未雨，防患未然；臨時又不能效命疆場
，率衆抵抗，而見後數年在抗日工作上，亦屬建樹毫無
；且因其缺乏遠見與定見，終致劫持 領袖，釀成西安
事變。縱然能遵中央的寬恕，却不能逃國人的清議。即

抗戰已達四年了，我們很多的土地與都市也化為灰燼陷於荒蕪更犧牲
了，許多不可復得的親愛的同胞。
然而所給與的代價是什麼？
中國歷史上未曾一見的饑餓與物質的不足，倒在路上餓在屋外的同胞
一天天地泛起來恰成了淒慘底地獄的一幅絕大描繪。

同胞們萬勿錯誤了目標呵！
必須將英美驅除了！

Office of the S.M.R. Co. and the Manchoukuan Trade
Representatives' Department in Shanghai, with the
support of the Shanghai Japanese Young Men's
Association, to commemorate the tenth anniversary

Shanghai Shinto Shrine. A large number of
military and civilian officials will attend.

Akiyama, Chief of the local Press Information
Department, and Mr. Ito, Chief of the
Shanghai Office of the S.M.R. Co., will
deliver addresses in the Shanghai Japanese
Young Men's Association building. This
will be followed by an exhibition of
moving pictures. Miss Ri Ko-ran, an
actress of the Manchou Film Co., who is now
in Shanghai, will give special performances
in the building.

adopt the necessary precautionary measures against
untoward incidents.

In the year of 1935, I obtained the driving permit.
In the year of 1940, I was employed by my master Tien
Sz Ming (錢時敏) of No. 34 Chien Tuh Faung, Yu Yuen Road
as a chauffeur to drive private m/car Lic. No. 3798.
At about 2p.m. 18/9/41, the m/car was parked in front
of the International Printing Works, 889-893 Sinza Road
which company has some relations with my master), when my
master said "These several persons want a car, and you can
take them to any place as they want." Those persons, about
four in number, some wearing Chinese clothing while some
wearing foreign clothing boarded the m/car. One of the
persons who had a bundle of paper (pamphlets) in his hand
told me to drive to the corner of Nanking and Shansi Roads.
I drove the car East along Sinza Road, turning south into
Carter Road and later east into B'Well Road and drove
straight along. They distributed the pamphlets along
B'Well Road. The m/car stopped at the corner of Nanking
and Shansi Road, and they alighted and went away. About
1 hour later, they all returned and boarded my car. They
then ordered me to take them to the printing company, on Sinza
Road which I did. At 6p.m. my master and two others boarded
the car, one of the two men named Au Tsung Moh bringing a
bundle of pamphlets with him. After they had boarded the
car, my master told me to drive to No. 34 Chien Tuh Faung,
Yu Yuen Road, but on arriving at the Yu Yuen Road Barrier,
the pamphlets were found by the police and we were brought to
the station.
J M Cakyss? The above is my true statement.

In the year of 193h, I obtained the driving permit.
In the year of 1940, I was employed by my master Hien
Sz Ying (錢時敏) of No. 34 Chien Tuh Faung, Yu Yuen Road
as a chauffeur to drive private m/car No. 3798.
At about 2p.m. 18/9/41, the m/car was parked in front
of the International Printing Works, 689-693 Sinsa Road
(which company has some relations with my master), when my
master said "these several persons want a car, and you can
take them to any place as they want." Those persons, about
four in number, some wearing Chinese clothing while some
wearing foreign clothing boarded the m/car. One of the
persons who had a bundle of paper (pamphlets) in his hand
told me to drive to the corner of Nanking and Shansi Roads.
I drove the car first along Sinsa Road, turning south into
Carter Road and later east into B'Well Road and drove
straight along. They distributed the pamphlets along
B'Well Road. The m/car stopped at the corner of Nanking
and Shansi Road, and they alighted and went away. About
1 hour later, they all returned and boarded my car. They
then ordered me to take them to the printing company, on Sinsa
Road which I did. At 4p.m. my master and two others boarded
the car, one of the two men named Au Yeung Ish bringing a
bundle of pamphlets with him. After they had boarded the
car, my master told me to drive to No. 34 Chien Tuh Faung,
Yu Yuen Road, but on arriving at the Yu Yuen Road Barrier,
the pamphlets were found by the police and we were brought to
the station.

The above is my true statement.
(sd.) Li Vung Nyoh.

18th. Sept. 1941.

Illegal Functioning of Japanese
Consular Official.
------------------------------------

Sir;

I beg to report that at about 8.30 a.m. 18-9-41 I
was walking south along Seymour Road toward Avenue Road
when I observed an untidily dressed Oriental dabbing a
tramway pole D.D.56 with some white substance, at the
same time stealthily looking on both sides of the road.
I came up towards him and saw three posters in Chinese
stuck on the poles. The posters were wet and looked as
they had just been stuck on. Believing the said
Oriental to have been responsible for the posting, I
told him I was a Police Officer and searched him to see
if he had any more posters on his person. Suddenly he
told me in Chinese that he was of Japanese nationality.
I then told him to come to the station where the matter
could be cleared. He, however, said that he had a
bicycle inside the Lane 470 Seymour Road (Pacific
Gardens). I went with him into the said lane and he
pointed out a motor cycle combination Lic. No.69. I
then telephoned to the Station asking to send a
Japanese Detective. At that time the Japanese said he
was from the Japanese Consulate and produced a permit
to drive m/cycle F.17"U" in the name of Fujio Uda, c/o
the Japanese Consulate.

A few minutes later D.S.777 Furukawa arrived and
spoke to the Japanese after which he told me that the
Japanese was a member of the Japanese Consulate Staff
and had been removing the posters which were of the
Anti-Japanese nature. I explained to D.S.777 Furukawa

日本领事官员的
非法行为。
------------------------------------

先生：

谨报告，1941年9月18日上午8时30分左右，我正沿西摩路（Seymour Road）向南朝爱文义路（Avenue Road）方向行走时，观察到一名衣着不整的东方人正在用某种白色物质涂抹电车杆 D.D.56，同时鬼鬼祟祟地观察道路两侧。我走近他，看到电线杆上贴有三张中文海报。海报是湿的，看起来像是刚贴上去的。我认为该东方人应对张贴行为负责，便告知他我是警察官员，并搜查他身上是否还有更多海报。突然，他用中文告诉我他是日本国籍。于是我让他去捕房，以便澄清此事。然而，他说他在西摩路470弄（太平洋花园）内有一辆自行车。我随他进入该弄堂，他指出一辆车牌号为69的组合摩托车。随后我打电话给捕房，要求派遣一名日本侦探。当时那名日本人说他来自日本领事馆，并出示了一张以宇田富士雄（Fujio Uda，转交日本领事馆）名义驾驶的摩托车执照 F.17"U"。

几分钟后，777号副巡官古川（Furukawa）到达，并与该日本人交谈，之后他告诉我，该日本人是日本领事馆工作人员，正在移除具有反日性质的海报。我向777号副巡官古川解释

pages.en:

that the correct procedure for Japanese if he saw any
posters, was to inform the S.M.P. who would have the
posters removed. I asked D.S.777 Furukawa to request
the Japanese to come to the Station where his identity
could be verified and the matter cleared, but this was
refused as D.S.777 Furukawa said that the Japanese
Consular Police was to be notified first. Leaving
D.S.777 Furukawa to carry out the "customary" procedure
I went to the Station and reported the incident to the
Officer i/c. and the Sen.-ior Detective. With a Station
Coolie I proceeded to Seymour Road and had all the
posters removed.

D. S. I.

Tsai Ding Chuen (崔鼎鈞)
Chinkiang // D.S.I. Lee Shu Fah
C.B.H.Q. 24-9-41

Tsai Ding Chuen, 17, Chinkiang, S/Apprentice, resid-
ing Lane 50, House 26 Anam Road, states:-
I was born in Chinkiang in 1925. After graduating
from primary school in 1938 I came to Shanghai to live with
my uncle Tsai Dh Fu. In November 1940 I obtained a position
as apprentice in F. J. Lutfy & Co., 81 Jinkee Road, where my
uncle also worked. I have held this position since.
At about 5.30 p.m. 15-9-41, when passing the corner
of Szechuen & Jinkee Roads, I saw a male Chinese riding in a
public ricksha throw away about 18 white slips of papers. I
picked them up and found printed on them a number of patriotic
slogans! I then telephoned to one Wang Sung Kung, whose
acquaintance I made whilst studying in an evening school in
1939, and asked him to come to Szechuen & Jinkee Roads corner.
I showed the handbills to Wang who took them away stating he
would have them posted up. We then posted.
In the afternoon of 16-9-41 some detectives came
to F. J. Lutfy & Co. and arrested me.
I have never distributed any handbills myself or
taken part in any political activities.

Signed:
pages.zh:
崔鼎鈞（Tsai Ding Chuen）
镇江 // 副巡官 李树法（Lee Shu Fah）
刑事科总部 1941年9月24日

崔鼎鈞，17岁，镇江人，商店学徒，居住于安南路（Anam Road）50弄26号，陈述如下：
我于1925年出生在镇江。1938年小学毕业后，我来上海与叔叔崔笃甫（Tsai Dh Fu）同住。1940年11月，我在金基路（Jinkee Road）81号的 F. J. Lutfy & Co. 获得了一份学徒职位，我的叔叔也在那里工作。此后我一直担任该职。
1941年9月15日下午5时30分左右，当我经过四川路与金基路转角时，我看到一名中国男子乘坐公共人力车扔掉了大约18张白色纸条。我捡起它们，发现上面印有许多爱国口号！随后我打电话给王松庚（Wang Sung Kung），我是1939年在夜校学习时认识他的，并请他到四川路与金基路转角处见面。我将传单给王看，他拿走传单，称他会将其张贴出去。随后我们进行了张贴。
1941年9月16日下午，几名侦探来到 F. J. Lutfy & Co. 并将我逮捕。
我从未亲自分发过任何传单，也未参与任何政治活动。

签名：

pages.en:
Loo Kwei mau (楼观涛)
mausing // D.S.I. Lee Shu Fah
C.B.H.Q. 24-9-41

Loo Kwei Mau, 17, maushing, S/Apprentice, residing
Lane 43, 28 Hart Road, states:-
I was born in Shanghai in 1925. From 1931 to 1936 I
studied in a primary school. In 1939 I went to study English
in an evening school where I became acquainted with Tsai Ding
Chuen and Maung Sung Kung. At present I am employed as an
apprentice by Dr. Lee Ching Wen, Room 403 B, International
Dispensary Building, Foochow Road.
At about 10.30 p.m. 15-9-41, after leaving the
evening school with my younger brother Loo Kwei Nyau, I met
Maung Sung Kung on Avenue Foch near Weihaiwei Road. Maung
asked my younger brother to hold a parcel, which I later found
to contain a bottle of paste, for him. Then Maung proceeded to
post some handbills on the wall. I took one down from the wall
in order to read it properly. I then pasted it back on the wall
and whilst doing so a policeman arrested me and the two others.
I have never before posted any political slogans or
taken part in any political activities.

Signed:
pages.zh:
楼观涛（Loo Kwei mau）
毛辛（mausing，原文不清，疑为地名或拼写错误）// 副巡官 李树法（Lee Shu Fah）
刑事科总部 1941年9月24日

楼观涛，17岁，毛辛人，商店学徒，居住于哈同路（Hart Road）43弄28号，陈述如下：
我于1925年出生在上海。1931年至1936年，我在小学读书。1939年，我去夜校学习英语，在那里认识了崔鼎鈞和汪商庚（Maung Sung Kung）。目前，我在福州路国际大药房大楼403 B室受雇于李经文（Lee Ching Wen）医生，担任学徒。
1941年9月15日晚上10时30分左右，我和弟弟楼观牛（Loo Kwei Nyau）离开夜校后，在福煦路（Avenue Foch）靠近威海卫路的地方遇到了汪商庚（Maung Sung Kung）。汪让我弟弟帮他拿一个包裹，后来我发现里面装着一瓶浆糊。然后汪开始在墙上张贴一些传单。我从墙上取下一张以便仔细阅读。随后我又将其贴回墙上，就在此时，一名警察逮捕了我及另外两人。
我以前从未张贴过任何政治标语，也未参与任何政治活动。

签名：

pages.en:
WOUNG SUNG FUNG (汪商庚)
Nanking                                /// D.S.I. Lee Shu Fah
C.B.H.Q.              24-9-41

WOUNG SUNG FUNG, 18, Nanking, S/Apprentice, residing
625 Szochuen Road, states:-

    I was born in Shanghai and attended a primary
school in Nantao for four years from 1932 to 1936. In 1939
I went to study English in an evening school where I became
acquainted with Tsai Ding Chuen and Loo Kwei Dau. At present
I am employed as an apprentice in the Ming Fong Co., a
Japanese concern, Room 312, Hardoon Building, Nanking Road.
    At about 7 p.m. 15-9-41 Tsai Ding Chuen telephoned
me and said he wished to see me at the corner of Szochuen and
Jinkee Roads. Upon arriving there I carried on a conversation
with Tsai in the course of which he gave me about 20 handbills
which he stated had been thrown from a ricksha. I put the hand-
bills in a book which I was carrying with the intention of
reading them later. I then left Tsai and went to the evening
school.
    At about 10 p.m. 15-9-41 after leaving school, I met
Loo Kwei Dau and his younger brother Loo Kwei Nyau on Avenue
Foch near Weihaiwei Road. I produced the handbills given me
by Tsai and after a discussion Loo Kwei Dau and I decided to post
them on the wall. We had posted two sheets when a plain-clothes
policeman arrested us. I managed to tear up the rest of the
handbills.
    I had never on any other occasion posted or distribu-
ted any political handbills.

                                    Signed:-
pages.zh:
汪商庚（WOUNG SUNG FUNG）
南京                                /// 副巡官 李树法（Lee Shu Fah）
刑事科总部              1941年9月24日

汪商庚，18岁，南京人，商店学徒，居住于四川路（Szochuen Road）625号，陈述如下：

    我出生在上海，1932年至1936年在南市的一所小学读了四年书。1939年，我去夜校学习英语，在那里认识了崔鼎鈞和楼灌涛（Loo Kwei Dau）。目前，我在南京路哈同大楼312室的明丰公司（Ming Fong Co.，一家日本公司）担任学徒。
    1941年9月15日晚上7点左右，崔鼎鈞给我打电话，说他想在四川路与金基路转角处见我。到达那里后，我与崔进行了交谈，期间他给了我大约20张传单，称这些传单是从一辆人力车上扔下来的。我把传单放进随身携带的一本书里，打算稍后阅读。随后我离开崔去了夜校。
    1941年9月15日晚上10点左右，离开学校后，我在福煦路靠近威海卫路的地方遇到了楼灌涛和他的弟弟楼观牛（Loo Kwei Nyau）。我拿出崔给我的传单，经过讨论，楼灌涛和我决定将它们贴在墙上。当我们贴了两张时，一名便衣警察逮捕了我们。我设法撕碎了剩余的传单。
    我此前从未在任何其他场合张贴或分发过任何政治传单。

                                    签名:-

Pamphlets circulated soliciting contributions
under the Conscientious Contribution Movement

With reference to the attached circular handed
into Louza Station by the D.C. Crime at about
6 p.m. the 15-9-41. It had been delivered to the
management of the Rialto Cinema, Peking and Kweichow
Roads. A rough translation reads as follows:-

"To the
Rialto Theatre,

It was on the 18th September, ten years
ago, when Japanese troops commenced invasion
of China's territory. Following the sounding
of the War Drum, the youths of the Chinese
Nation arose and carried out their historical
and sacred salvation work. Chinese soldiers
battled in the war front despite the wind and r
rain, and disregarded death, whatsoever.
Citizens at the rear also themselves controlled
endured; naturally every body should shoulder
responsibility for the nation's prosperity
or otherwise.
During the time of war, it is found that
your theatre has rendered no assistance to
your own country, but has made much money
by taking advantage. Approximately estimating
that your earnings are thousands and thousands
more than previous.
Now the 10th Anniversary of "September 18th"
is approaching, and for the purpose of spread-
ing patriotic idea among we Chinese, and also
a heavy moral and spiritual strike at the
enemy, we suggest that the "Conscientious
Contribution Movements" be formed, and would
like to express your sympathy.
Prior to the date - September 18th - we
invite you to contribute $918.00 to the
office of the Chinese-American Daily News
under the name of "Tseu I Mang" (鄒憶孟).
The money will afterwards be distributed by
the recipient.
Apart from taking drastic measure against
you, should you fail to do so, we must find
a way of compelling you to carry out our
bidding at any time, date, and place.
Chopped:-Tsen-yi Association.
( 正義社 )
N.B. To avoid misunderstanding, please use the
name "Tseu I Mang" when contributing the
money"

流传要求为“良心捐献运动”捐款的传单

参照附件通告，该通告由刑事科副督察长于1941年9月15日下午6时许送至卢家嘴捕房。它已被送达北京路与贵州路里亚尔托电影院的管理处。粗略翻译如下：

“致
里亚尔托剧院，

十年前的9月18日，日军开始入侵中国领土。随着战鼓敲响，中国青年奋起，开展了他们历史性的神圣救亡工作。中国士兵在前线浴血奋战，不顾风雨，视死如归。后方民众也自我克制，忍受苦难；自然每个人都应承担国家兴衰的责任。
在战争期间，发现贵剧院未对自己的国家提供任何援助，反而利用局势赚取了大量金钱。粗略估计，你们的收入比之前多出成千上万倍。
现在‘九一八’十周年纪念日即将来临，为了在我们中国人中传播爱国思想，并对敌人给予沉重的道德和精神打击，我们建议成立‘良心捐献运动’，并希望表达你们的同情。
在9月18日之前，我们邀请你们以‘邹忆孟’（Tseu I Mang）的名义，向《中美日报》办事处捐款918.00元。
这笔钱随后将由接收方进行分配。
如果你们不这样做，除了对你们采取严厉措施外，我们必须随时、随地、以任何方式强迫你们执行我们的命令。
盖章：正义社。
( 正義社 )
注意：为避免误解，捐款时请使用‘邹忆孟’这个名字”

insertions when roughly translated, as follows:-

No. 1
"To be noted by contributors of "Conscientious
Contributions"

The motive of this Daily's acceptance of
the "Conscientious Contributions" is originally
with the hope that readers be conscientious and
contribute monetary gifts. The Daily serves
for the readers who offer voluntary contributions,
no slight force to be used in this direction.
Since accepting such contributions ranging from
$0.10 to $10,000.00, the Daily has up to the
present received a total amount, exceeding
$100,000.00. This proved the human conscience,
which resulted in readers' fervent contributions.
Many of the Daily's enthusiastic readers apart
from their own contribution solicit in re.
We welcome readers' self contributions and

using force. We will not be agreeable to
those who solicit contributions by means of
